segments.say: And somewhere in your drifting, the train slows one last time, and stops at a tiny station deep in a forest. You step down onto the platform, wrapped in your warm blanket. The air smells of pine and rain. The train glides softly away into the dark. And a narrow path leads from the platform, between the tall trees, toward a small light glowing a little way off.

It's raining gently. Not a storm, just a soft and steady rain, falling through the branches overhead. You can hear it on the leaves, a quiet, endless whisper. The path is soft beneath your feet, covered in old pine needles. And the little light ahead grows warmer and closer as you walk, slowly, with no hurry at all.

Picture the cabin as it appears between the trees. Small and wooden, with a sloping roof shining wet in the rain. Warm golden light glowing in its windows. A thin trail of smoke rising from the chimney. And a mossy path leading right up to the door, as if the cabin had been expecting you all along.

You open the door and step inside. A fire is already crackling in a little stone fireplace. There's a soft armchair beside it, with a thick knitted blanket. A kettle sits on a small stove, just beginning to murmur. Everything is warm, and quiet, and ready. You take off your wet shoes and sink into the armchair, and the warmth of the fire wraps around you.

Above you, the rain patters on the wooden roof. A soft, uneven drumming, never loud, never quite the same twice. Some drops land close, right overhead. Others sound farther away, on the edge of the eaves. Together, they make one of the most soothing sounds in the world. You can just listen to it, and let it carry your thoughts away.

Listen to the cabin around you. Rain on the roof. The fire, crackling and settling. The kettle, murmuring softly on the stove. And outside, the wind moving gently through the tall pines, a long, slow sigh. Every sound is soft. Every sound is calm. And together, they make a quiet song that asks nothing of you at all.

The kettle sings, softly, and you pour yourself a cup of tea. You wrap both hands around the warm cup and breathe in the steam. It smells of honey and something sweet and herbal. You take a slow sip. The warmth spreads from your hands, up your arms, and into your chest. You set the cup down beside you, and lean back into the chair.

Here's a thought for the cabin. Nothing to finish. Nothing to fix. There are no tasks waiting in this little room, no messages to answer, no plans to make. The rain will keep falling whether you watch it or not. The fire will keep glowing. And you can simply be here, resting, with nothing at all expected of you.

show.text: Nothing to finish. Nothing to fix.

segments.say: You watch the fire for a while. The flames move slowly, curling and flickering, orange and gold. A log shifts and settles with a soft sigh, sending up a few tiny sparks that drift and fade. The light dances on the wooden walls. Watching a fire like this, time seems to slow right down, until there's only the flicker, and the warmth, and the rain.

Your body feels heavier now, sinking deeper into the soft armchair. Your arms rest on the arms of the chair. Your feet are warm by the fire. The knitted blanket is soft around your shoulders. Your eyelids are getting heavy. And every sound in the cabin, the rain, the fire, the wind, seems to be saying the same gentle thing. Rest now. Rest.

Picture the corner by the fire. The soft armchair. The knitted blanket draped across it. A cup of tea steaming on a little table. And behind it all, the dark window, streaked with gentle rain. It's the coziest corner you can imagine. A small, warm place in a big, quiet forest, where the night can't reach you at all.

Let your breathing slow down with the rain. In, softly, as the drops patter on the roof. Out, slowly, as the sound blurs into a gentle hush. In. And out. You don't need to count anymore. The rain is keeping time for you, steady and kind. And each breath brings you a little deeper into rest.

There's a book resting on your lap. You don't remember picking it up, and you don't need to read it. Its pages are soft and old. Perhaps it's full of stories, or poems, or quiet pictures. But tonight, it can stay closed. Just feel its gentle weight, and let your hands rest on its cover. Some nights are for reading. This night is for rest.

show.cap: A book you don't need to read

segments.say: Let's gather the cabin together. A crackling fire. A warm cup of tea. A closed book on your lap. Rain on the roof. And your slow, easy breath. Everything is calm here. Everything is soft. You can stay as long as you like. The night is long, and kind, and there's plenty of time.

After a while, the rain grows softer. The drumming on the roof fades to a light patter, then to a faint whisper, then almost to silence. Just the occasional drop, falling from the eaves. The fire has burned down to a warm glow. The cabin is very, very quiet now. And somewhere outside, the clouds are beginning to part.

Through the window, a little silver light appears. The moon is peeking out from behind the clouds, shining on the wet branches, making the raindrops glitter. It's beautiful, and calm. And you feel a gentle wish to step outside, just for a moment, wrapped in your blanket, to see the garden behind the cabin, glowing under the moon. There's no hurry. When you're ready, we'll go.
